candidates.label: acquiredFrom
candidates.comment: An acquired from relation between ownership information and the organization or person from whom a product was obtained. Also called purchased from, obtained from, source of acquisition. Examples: "The car's ownership info indicates it was acquired from 'Dealership X'.", "The book's ownership info shows it was acquired from 'John Doe'."

candidates.label: purchaseDate
candidates.comment: A purchase date relation between a product or vehicle and the date it was acquired by its current owner. Also called acquired on, bought on, ownership date. Examples: "A car has a purchase date of 2020-05-10.", "A smartphone has a purchase date of 2023-01-15.", "A house has a purchase date of 2018-07-22.". Distinct from productionDate, which is the date the item was manufactured.

candidates.label: buyer
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sell action, indicating the organization or person who purchased the object. Also called "purchaser", "customer", "acquired by". Examples: "Online purchase sell action buyer Jane Doe", "Company acquisition sell action buyer Acme Corp". Distinct from seller, which is the party offering the object for sale.

candidates.label: ownedFrom
candidates.comment: The date and time when ownership of a product was obtained. Also called acquisition date, purchase date, date acquired. Examples: "Car OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2020-01-15'", "House OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2018-06-01T10:00:00'", "Book OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2023-03-10'". Distinct from ownedThrough, which is the date ownership ended.

candidates.label: owner
candidates.comment: A person or organization that owns a thing. Also called proprietor, possessor, title holder. Examples: "Car owner 'John Doe'", "Company owner 'Acme Corp'", "House owner 'Smith Family Trust'". Distinct from creator, who made the thing.

candidates.label: acquireLicensePage
candidates.comment: An acquire license page relation between a creative work and the web page or resource detailing how its licenses can be obtained. Also called licensing information page, purchase license URL, rights acquisition page. Examples: "A stock photo's acquire license page is its licensing terms URL.", "A software's acquire license page describes its purchase options."

candidates.label: owns
candidates.comment: A thing that is owned by an organization or person. Also called possesses, holds title to, has ownership of. Examples: "John Doe owns 'a car'", "Acme Corp owns 'a patent'", "Sarah owns 'her house'". Distinct from memberOf, which describes membership in a group.

candidates.label: purchaseType
candidates.comment: A purchase type relation between a financial incentive and the specific kind of purchase required to qualify for it. Also called qualifying purchase, incentive purchase type. Examples: "A cashback offer requires a purchase type 'new customer'.", "A loyalty discount requires a purchase type 'repeat purchase'.", "A promotional offer requires a purchase type 'online only'."

candidates.label: vendor
candidates.comment: A vendor relation between a buy action and the organization or person selling the item. Also called seller, merchant, supplier. Examples: "BuyAction vendor 'Amazon'", "BuyAction vendor 'Local Bookstore'", "BuyAction vendor 'John Doe'". Distinct from seller, which is the current preferred term.

candidates.label: isGift
candidates.comment: A transaction intent relation indicating whether an order was placed as a gift for a recipient other than the buyer. Also called gift purchase, purchased as gift, gift order. Examples: An order has isGift set to 'true'. A purchase has isGift set to 'false'. A book order has isGift set to 'true' with gift wrapping.

relations.definition: To work together in a business or activity.
relations.embedding_query_text: partner: To work together in a business or activity.

candidates.label: spouse
candidates.comment: A marital relation between two persons who are married to each other. Also called "husband", "wife", "married to", "partner". Examples: "John has spouse Jane", "Mary's spouse is David", "The couple includes a spouse relationship.". Distinct from colleague, which indicates a professional relationship, or parent, which indicates a familial relationship.

candidates.label: colleagues
candidates.comment: A professional relation between a person and other persons who are their colleagues. Also called "co-workers", "associates", "professional peers". Examples: "John colleagues [Jane, Peter]", "Mary colleagues [Sarah, Tom]". Distinct from colleague, which is a singular form, though semantically similar.

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: employee
candidates.comment: An employment relation between an organization and a person who works for it. Also called "works for", "staff member", "on staff". Examples: "Organization 'Google' employee 'Sundar Pichai'", "Company 'Acme Corp' employee 'Jane Doe'", "Restaurant 'The Bistro' employee 'Chef John'". Distinct from member, which indicates a general affiliation rather than an employment relationship.

candidates.label: colleague
candidates.comment: A professional relation between a person and another person who is their colleague. Also called "co-worker", "associate", "professional peer". Examples: "John colleague Jane", "Professor Smith colleague 'https://example.com/prof-jones'". Distinct from colleagues, which is a plural form, though semantically similar.

candidates.label: worksFor
candidates.comment: An employment relation between a person and an organization, indicating the organization for which the person is employed. Also called employed by, affiliated with, works at, employed at. Examples: Employee worksFor CompanyA, Consultant worksFor AgencyB, Professor worksFor UniversityC. Distinct from memberOf, which indicates general membership in a group, not necessarily employment.

candidates.label: eligibleWithSupplier
candidates.comment: An eligible with supplier relation between a financial incentive and the organization that supplies the incentivized item or service. Also called "supplier partner", "incentive provider", "valid with retailer". Examples: "Rebate eligibleWithSupplier 'Utility Company X'", "Discount eligibleWithSupplier 'Electronics Store Y'", "Grant eligibleWithSupplier 'Solar Panel Installer Z'".

candidates.label: broker
candidates.comment: An intermediary relation between an invoice, order, reservation, or service and the organization or person who arranges the exchange. Also called "arranged by", "intermediary", "agent". Examples: "Flight reservation broker Expedia", "Real estate service broker John Doe", "Stock order broker Fidelity". Distinct from seller or buyer, which indicate direct parties in an exchange, whereas broker facilitates it without taking ownership.

candidates.label: funder
candidates.comment: A funder relation between a creative work, event, grant, organization, or person and the organization or person providing financial support or sponsorship. Also called: sponsor, benefactor, financial supporter. Examples: "Art Exhibition" funder "National Endowment for the Arts", "Research Project" funder "NIH", "Charity Event" funder "Local Bank". Distinct from fundedItem, which is the item receiving funding.

candidates.label: makesOffer
candidates.comment: An offering relation between an organization or person and the offer for products or services they provide. Also called: offers, provides, sells. Examples: "Retailer makesOffer Discounted Electronics", "Consultant makesOffer Business Strategy Services", "Restaurant makesOffer Dinner Menu".

candidates.label: merchant

candidates.label: availableAtOrFrom

candidates.label: category

candidates.label: businessFunction

candidates.label: studySubject

candidates.label: study

Examples: "The drug has study a clinical trial", "The medical condition is part of a study", "This therapy is being evaluated in a study."

candidates.label: question

candidates.label: ethicsPolicy

Also called "code of ethics", "conduct policy", "ethical guidelines". Examples: "News media organization ethicsPolicy 'example.com/ethics'", "Restaurant ethicsPolicy 'Statement on sustainable sourcing'", "Company ethicsPolicy 'CreativeWork detailing corporate values'". Distinct from diversityPolicy, which specifically addresses diversity and inclusion.

candidates.label: studyLocation

Also called "research location", "trial site", "study area", "geographic scope of study". Examples: "The medical study has studyLocation New York", "The clinical trial's studyLocation is Europe", "This study is taking place in a specific studyLocation."

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: assesses
candidates.comment: A relation between a creative work, education event, or learning resource and the competency or learning outcome it is intended to evaluate. Examples: "LearningResource 'Quiz' assesses 'Understanding of Algebra'", "EducationEvent 'Exam' assesses 'Problem-solving skills'", "CreativeWork 'Rubric' assesses 'Writing proficiency'."

candidates.label: studyDesign

Examples: "The study has studyDesign CohortStudy", "The medical observational study's studyDesign is CrossSectionalStudy", "This research uses a studyDesign of CaseControlStudy."

candidates.label: participant

candidates.label: claimInterpreter

candidates.label: sponsor

candidates.label: fundedItem

candidates.label: lender

candidates.label: amount

candidates.label: beneficiaryBank

candidates.label: borrower

chosen_property.label: reports

candidates.label: description

candidates.label: reportNumber

candidates.label: disambiguatingDescription

candidates.label: dateline

candidates.label: accessibilitySummary

candidates.label: bookEdition

candidates.label: reservationStatus

candidates.label: isAcceptingNewPatients
candidates.comment: A patient status relation indicating whether a medical organization is currently accepting new patients. Also called accepting new patients, open to new patients, taking new patients. Examples: A clinic has isAcceptingNewPatients set to 'true'. A hospital has isAcceptingNewPatients set to 'false'. A doctor's office has isAcceptingNewPatients set to 'true'.

candidates.label: recognizingAuthority
candidates.comment: A recognizing authority relation between a medical entity and the organization that officially endorses it within a system of medicine. Also called endorsed by, officially recognized by. Examples: "A medical treatment is recognized by 'the World Health Organization'.", "A medical specialty is recognized by 'the American Medical Association'.", "A traditional medicine practice is recognized by 'a national health ministry'."

candidates.label: isLiveBroadcast
candidates.comment: A broadcast status relation indicating whether a broadcast event is being transmitted in real-time. Also called live stream, real-time broadcast, live transmission. Examples: A sports game broadcast has isLiveBroadcast set to 'true'. A news report broadcast has isLiveBroadcast set to 'true'. A recorded TV show broadcast has isLiveBroadcast set to 'false'.

candidates.label: validIn
candidates.comment: A valid in relation between a certification, credential, or permit and the geographic area where it is valid. Also called valid region, applicable area, geographic validity. Examples: "Permit validIn 'California'", "Certification validIn 'European Union'", "Credential validIn 'United States'".

candidates.label: certificationStatus
candidates.comment: A status relation for a certification, indicating whether it is active or inactive. Also called "certificate status", "certification validity", "status of certification". Examples: "Product certification certificationStatus Active", "Company certification certificationStatus Inactive".

candidates.label: acceptsReservations
candidates.comment: A reservation acceptance status indicating whether a food establishment allows bookings. Also called takes reservations, booking available, reservation policy. Examples: "A restaurant accepts reservations is true.", "The cafe accepts reservations via its website URL.", "This diner accepts reservations is 'No'."

candidates.label: suggestedAnswer
candidates.comment: A proposed response or set of responses to a question. Also called "possible answer", "proposed solution", "answer option", "response to question". Examples: "The question has suggestedAnswer 'Yes'", "The quiz question's suggestedAnswer is a multiple-choice list", "This question provides a suggestedAnswer for users."

chosen_property.label: needsApprovalFrom
chosen_property.definition: To require official permission or consent from someone or something.

candidates.label: expectsAcceptanceOf
candidates.comment: An expects acceptance of relation between an action access specification, consume action, or media subscription and an offer that must be accepted before the action can be performed. Also called: requires offer, prerequisite offer, conditional offer. Examples: "Watch Movie Action" expects acceptance of "Movie Purchase Offer", "Download Software Action" expects acceptance of "Software License Offer", "Access Premium Content" expects acceptance of "Subscription Offer".

candidates.label: permissions
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute detailing the permissions required for a software application to function. Also called access requirements, app permissions, authorization needs. Examples: A mobile app requires permissions for 'full internet access'. A software application requires permissions for 'access to camera'. A game requires permissions for 'storage access'.

candidates.label: requiresSubscription
candidates.comment: A subscription requirement relation indicating whether an action access or media object necessitates a subscription for use. Also called subscription needed, paywall, access restriction. Examples: "A streaming movie requires subscription 'true'.", "A news article requires subscription 'false'.", "A premium feature requires subscription 'true'."

candidates.label: eligibilityToWorkRequirement
candidates.comment: An eligibility to work requirement relation between a job posting and the text describing the legal documentation needed for an applicant. Also called "work authorization", "visa requirements", "employment eligibility". Examples: "Job posting eligibilityToWorkRequirement 'Must be authorized to work in the US'", "Job eligibilityToWorkRequirement 'Valid work permit required'", "Job eligibilityToWorkRequirement 'EU citizenship or valid visa'".

candidates.label: issuedBy
candidates.comment: An issuing authority relation between a certification, permit, or ticket and the organization that granted or provided it. Also called granted by, provided by, authorized by, issuer. Examples: A driver's license is issuedBy 'Department of Motor Vehicles'. A concert ticket is issuedBy 'Ticketmaster'. A professional certification is issuedBy 'Certification Body X'.

candidates.label: actionAccessibilityRequirement
candidates.comment: An action accessibility requirement relation between a consume action and the specifications that must be met to perform it. Also called action prerequisites, access conditions, fulfillment requirements. Examples: "A 'watch movie' action's accessibility requirement is 'subscription'.", "A 'download software' action's accessibility requirement is 'login'."

candidates.label: validFrom
candidates.comment: A valid from relation between a certification, demand, financial incentive, location feature specification, monetary amount, offer, opening hours specification, permit, or price specification and the date it becomes valid. Also called effective date, start date, activation date. Examples: "Offer validFrom '2023-11-01'", "Permit validFrom '2023-01-01T09:00:00'", "OpeningHoursSpecification validFrom '2024-01-01'". Distinct from validThrough or validUntil, which specify the end of validity.

candidates.label: carrierRequirements
candidates.comment: A description of specific carrier requirements for a mobile application. Also called "network compatibility", "mobile operator requirements", "carrier restrictions". Examples: "Mobile app carrierRequirements 'Requires AT&T network'", "Messaging app carrierRequirements 'Works on all major carriers'".

candidates.label: browserRequirements
candidates.comment: A description of browser requirements for a web application. Also called "browser compatibility", "required browser features". Examples: "Online banking app browserRequirements 'Requires Chrome 80+ or Firefox 75+'", "Video streaming service browserRequirements 'Supports HTML5 video and DRM'".

candidates.label: issuedThrough
candidates.comment: A service channel relation between a permit and the specific service used to obtain it. Also called obtained via, granted through, service channel. Examples: A building permit was issuedThrough 'Online Permit Application System'. A fishing license was issuedThrough 'State Wildlife Service'. A visa was issuedThrough 'Consular Services Department'. Distinct from issuedBy, which is the organization, not the service.

candidates.label: owns
candidates.comment: A thing that is owned by an organization or person. Also called possesses, holds title to, has ownership of. Examples: "John Doe owns 'a car'", "Acme Corp owns 'a patent'", "Sarah owns 'her house'". Distinct from memberOf, which describes membership in a group.

candidates.label: owner
candidates.comment: A person or organization that owns a thing. Also called proprietor, possessor, title holder. Examples: "Car owner 'John Doe'", "Company owner 'Acme Corp'", "House owner 'Smith Family Trust'". Distinct from creator, who made the thing.

candidates.label: ownedFrom
candidates.comment: The date and time when ownership of a product was obtained. Also called acquisition date, purchase date, date acquired. Examples: "Car OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2020-01-15'", "House OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2018-06-01T10:00:00'", "Book OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2023-03-10'". Distinct from ownedThrough, which is the date ownership ended.

candidates.label: copyrightHolder
candidates.comment: A legal ownership relation between a creative work and the person or organization holding its copyright. Also called: copyright owner, rights holder, legally owned by. Examples: "The Mona Lisa" copyright holder "The Louvre Museum", "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone" copyright holder "J.K. Rowling", "Microsoft Windows" copyright holder "Microsoft Corporation".

candidates.label: ownedThrough
candidates.comment: The date and time when ownership of a product was relinquished. Also called disposal date, date sold, ownership end date. Examples: "Car OwnershipInfo ownedThrough '2023-05-20'", "House OwnershipInfo ownedThrough '2022-11-30T16:00:00'", "Book OwnershipInfo ownedThrough '2024-01-01'". Distinct from ownedFrom, which is the date ownership began.

candidates.label: landlord
candidates.comment: A property ownership relation between a rent action and the person or organization that owns and leases the real estate. Also called property owner, lessor, rental owner, proprietor. Examples: A rent action has a landlord of 'John Doe'. A rent action has a landlord of 'Property Management Inc.'. A lease agreement lists 'Sarah Smith' as the landlord. Distinct from agent, which is the general actor of an action.

candidates.label: numberOfPreviousOwners
candidates.comment: The total number of previous owners of a vehicle, including the current owner. Also called prior owners, owner history count, past owners. Examples: "Used Car A numberOfPreviousOwners 1", "Vintage Vehicle B numberOfPreviousOwners 3", "New Car C numberOfPreviousOwners 0".

candidates.label: ownershipFundingInfo
candidates.comment: Information describing the ownership structure, funding, and grants of an organization, particularly concerning editorial independence for news media. Also called funding transparency, ownership structure, financial backing details. Examples: "News Org A ownershipFundingInfo 'https://news.example.com/about/funding'", "Company B ownershipFundingInfo 'Privately held by XYZ Group.'", "Nonprofit C ownershipFundingInfo 'Funded by grants from various foundations.'". Distinct from funder, which specifically identifies the entity providing funds.

candidates.label: purchaseDate
candidates.comment: A purchase date relation between a product or vehicle and the date it was acquired by its current owner. Also called acquired on, bought on, ownership date. Examples: "A car has a purchase date of 2020-05-10.", "A smartphone has a purchase date of 2023-01-15.", "A house has a purchase date of 2018-07-22.". Distinct from productionDate, which is the date the item was manufactured.

candidates.label: acquiredFrom
candidates.comment: An acquired from relation between ownership information and the organization or person from whom a product was obtained. Also called purchased from, obtained from, source of acquisition. Examples: "The car's ownership info indicates it was acquired from 'Dealership X'.", "The book's ownership info shows it was acquired from 'John Doe'."
